title: What GPT-OSS actually means
oneliner: GPT-OSS = OpenAI's open-source models: 120B parameters for enterprises with serious infrastructure, 20B for lighter use.
says: OpenAI released two open models: GPT-OSS 120B and GPT-OSS 20B. He decodes the name: GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer, OSS for open-source software, and the numbers are billions of training parameters. The 120B model targets enterprise applications and needs heavy resources; the 20B is the lighter option.
explained: The name decoding is the useful part. Every model name is compressed information: the family (GPT), the license posture (OSS - weights you can download and run yourself), and the size (parameters are the model's learned dials; more parameters generally means more capability and much more hardware).

The size choice is an architecture decision, not a flex. A 120B-parameter model needs multiple high-end GPUs just to load, and its running cost follows. A 20B model fits on a fraction of that. His advice - enterprises explore the big one, others the small - is really about matching model size to the actual workload, a theme he expands later in his inference-economy reels. Open weights also change who controls your AI: you can host it yourself, which matters for data privacy and becomes central in his private-model-hosting episode in Season 1.
takeaway: Model names encode the decision: family, openness, size. Bigger is not better - match parameter count to the workload and the hardware you actually have.
